purpose: Compare two approved property timeline events in a citizen-readable way, identifying supported differences, affected interests, evidence and causation status without assuming that temporal sequence proves legal causation.
core_principle: EVENT A → EVENT DIFFERENCE → AFFECTED INTEREST → EVIDENCE → CAUSATION STATUS → EVENT B
rules: Both events must belong to the same verified property scope unless a separate comparison type authorises otherwise.
Temporal sequence alone does not establish causation.
Different event types do not necessarily imply different legal effects.
Each event retains its own event, document, registration and legal-effect dates.
A change in one property interest does not imply a change in another.
Party participation is compared as role evidence, not automatically as ownership.
Causal connection is shown only when independently supported.
Historical legal versions remain tied to their respective event dates.
Restricted evidence and private data remain protected.
hard_stops: Never infer causation because Event B happened after Event A.
Never infer ownership change from event-type difference alone.
Never merge document date with event or registration date.
Never treat party appearance as proof of legal role.
Never hide an unresolved causal conflict.
Never use current law to explain an earlier event without temporal verification.
Never create a new legal conclusion merely from comparison.
